title: Hosted API demo: embeddings + rerank - AcmeSearch
summary: Redwood AE+SE ran a hosted API demo for AcmeSearch focused on embeddings + reranking for improving search relevance. Discussed end-to-end flow: ingest -> embeddings -> vector store vs Redwood rerank endpoint, integration patterns, tuning (top_k, similarity metric), latency/cost tradeoffs, and security questions (SOC2, SSO, VPC/private options). Agreed next steps: send pricing, share security pack, provide quick benchmark harness and two-week PoC scope doc.
next_steps: Jordan to send hosted pricing + sample billing projection (by 2028-09-22)
Priya to share step-by-step quickstart + Postman collection and sample code (by 2028-09-22)
Jordan to share SOC2 + security pack and KMS notes (by 2028-09-23)
Schedule a 30-min PoC scoping call w/ engineering (tentative week of 2028-09-25)
action_items: Jordan Lee: Send pricing + projected monthly cost for 50M tokens and 10M embeddings - due 2028-09-22
Priya Patel: Share quick benchmark harness and sample rerank payloads - due 2028-09-22
Maria Gomez: Provide a representative query set and 1k labeled relevance pairs - due 2028-09-24
transcript:
Header: 2028-09-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45 mins | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Patel (Redwood) — Maria Gomez, Liam O'Connor, Nina Park (AcmeSearch)

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, ae on this account, and priya our solutions engineer is here to walk through the embeddings + rerank flow. quick check — audio ok?
00:10 Maria: yeah loud and clear, thank you.
00:14 Jordan: awesome. quick agenda: high level architecture, demo of hosted embeddings endpoint, then rerank endpoint and relevance walkthrough, and then q&a around security and deployment options. sound good?
00:24 Maria: perfect.
00:27 Priya: ok i'll share my screen, shout if the deck glitches. i want to emphasize we focus on hosted API first — low friction, quick benchmarks, and later you can move to dedicated or private if you need VPC.
01:02 Priya: (screen) here is the simple pipeline we recommend: ingest documents -> chunking -> call /embeddings to get vectors -> store in your vector DB (pinecone, elastic with vectors, or your own) -> candidate retrieval -> call our /rerank endpoint to apply a learned reranker on top to reorder the top_k results.
01:30 Nina: quick q — why not just use k-nearest on embeddings and call it a day?
01:37 Priya: great question. embeddings retrieval gives a good semantic candidate set but sometimes the top candidate order doesn't match business relevance — rerank lets you use the full-context model to score the candidates with the query, metadata, and other signals. we've seen lift of 8-25% in nDCG on ecom datasets compared to rank-by-similarity alone.
02:05 Liam: what's the latency hit for rerank? we have p95 target ~350ms for search.
02:12 Priya: for hosted rerank, p95 for a 10-candidate rerank is typically in the 120-220ms range depending on model size and tokenization; you'll add retrieval time on top. we showed earlier that with a small cross-encoder style model on our infra you can hit your 350ms target. there are knobs — batching, async user-visible streaming, and you can pick lighter models for faster latencies. note: numbers are approximate and we'll run a quick benchmark for your queries.
02:46 Maria: you mentioned model choice — is this running open models or something redwood provides?
02:52 Jordan: we host curated open models and provide verified performance profiles; customers can also bring their own models to Dedicated/Private. for Hosted API we offer a few default rerank-capable models; priya will show the API calls.
03:09 Priya: ok demo time. i'll switch to terminal; first, embeddings call: POST /v1/embeddings with document text, returns vector. example payload — note the model param, top_k not used here — you store resulting vector.
03:27 Priya (terminal): example response: embedding:[0.0023, -0.12, ...] — transcription note: vector values are truncated in the transcript.
03:40 Priya: then retrieval in your vector store, get top 50 candidates by cosine or dot. we typically recommend cosine for normalized vectors, dot for un-normalized.
04:00 Priya: now rerank call: POST /v1/rerank with query and list of candidate docs (title, snippet, metadata). the payload size matters because we send full context to the reranker. here's a sample where we send top_k:10 and the model returns per-document score and normalized rank.
04:23 Maria: are there size limits for the rerank payload? we have long product descriptions.
04:29 Priya: we support chunking — you can send either concatenated candidate snippets or compressed highlights. for very long docs we recommend summarizing or sending metadata plus snippet. also our SDKs support automatic truncation with prioritized fields.
04:52 Liam: what's the per-request cost model? tokens? embeddings units?
04:57 Jordan: hosted pricing is per-embedding unit and per-token for rerank. i'll send a sample projection after this call. typical approach: do cheap vector retrieval for 90% of requests and reserve rerank for top_x traffic or only for ambiguous queries to save cost.
05:18 Priya: demo result — here's before/after: baseline embedding retrieval ranking, then rerank output which moves commercially relevant items higher, you can see scores. small transcription glitch: the demo included live scoring and we toggled top_k from 10 to 20.
05:40 Nina: can we include business signals like recency or CTR?
05:44 Priya: yes, you can pass metadata per candidate and we include it in scoring. you can also add a re-weighting rule in the rerank payload to boost recency or sponsored items.
05:58 Maria: how do you handle A/B tests and rollouts?
06:03 Jordan: via Redwood Console — you can define routes, experiments, and split traffic between models or rerank policies, and view per-route latency/cost and token breakdowns. we can demo that in a follow-up.
06:21 Maria: security stuff: SOC2, SSO, data residency?
06:25 Jordan: yes SOC2, we have SAML SSO and RBAC. for data residency or stricter controls, Dedicated and Private deployments support VPC and on-prem. i'll attach the security pack.
06:40 Liam: customer data logging — are queries stored? KMS?
06:46 Jordan: you control retention settings; for Hosted we retain logs for X days by default and you can opt into longer retention for analytics. for encryption at rest we integrate with KMS/HSM for Private. i'll include the KMS notes.
07:00 Priya: moving back to technical details — embedding model comparators: we provide a few vector models tuned for search; differences are dimensionality, cost, and recall. we can run trials to pick the best for your corpus.
07:20 Maria: what's the integration effort? our stack is Node + Elastic for indexing, and we use Kubernetes.
07:25 Priya: you can call the hosted API directly from your backend; typical flow is an ingestion job that produces embeddings then stores in your vector store and elastic for metadata. retrieval hits vector store, then we call rerank for top_k. we'll share a sample Node snippet and a Postman collection.
07:48 Priya: quick code snippet: const res = await fetch('/v1/embeddings', {model: 'rw-embed-2'}); — again sample only.
08:02 Nina: any recommended top_k defaults?
08:05 Priya: we commonly use retrieving 50 then reranking top 10-20. number depends on recall required and latency budget.
08:15 Liam: how do you measure quality? we have labeled pair sets for our main vertical.
08:20 Priya: bring your labeled set — we can run nDCG tests. for PoC we ask for 1k queries with labels; you mentioned you have that, maria?
08:28 Maria: yes we can share a subset.
08:30 Priya: perfect. we'll run the harness and show before/after metrics.
08:36 Jordan: just to call out cost controls — Redwood Optimize will recommend batching, caching, and quantization options once we see patterns. for hosted mode, caching prefix hits is automatic for repeated queries.
08:55 Maria: caching — is it per-tenant? what about PII?
08:58 Jordan: caches are per-tenant in Hosted and respect retention and redaction rules. sensitive fields can be excluded. we'll include the docs.
09:10 Priya: demo: example rerank response payload shows per-doc score, normalizedrank, and a short explanation string. note transcripts sometimes show explanation as 'delta' in the UI.
09:30 Maria: can the reranker incorporate signals from user history?
09:34 Priya: yes, you can include user context in the rerank call; just be mindful of payload size and PII handling. you can hash or tokenize identifiers.
09:50 Liam: throughput concerns — what if we have bursts?
09:54 Jordan: Hosted autoscaling handles bursts within fair use, but for guaranteed throughput Dedicated reserved pools are better. we can propose a hybrid: hosted for development and lower traffic segments, dedicated for peak-critical endpoints.
10:10 Priya: ok i'll show a quick live ranking change with a real query from your dataset (demo data anonymized). Query: "best waterproof hiking boots for trail" — embedding retrieval returned 50 candidates; rerank moved 3 product pages with recent 5-star reviews to top.
10:40 Maria: nice. can you export the rerank scores back into elastic for analytics?
10:45 Priya: yes we return scores and metadata, you can store those fields back into elastic. many customers store final rank and score for downstream analytics and training.
11:00 Jordan: timecheck — we're at 11 minutes into the call (note: timestamps in transcript reflect segment times, not realtime). we'll speed up through the remaining demo.
11:10 Priya: notes on metrics: baseline recall, nDCG, click-through improvements, and p95 latency are our main success metrics. we'll help you instrument these in the PoC.
11:28 Maria: what about competitor integrations? we already use Pinecone for vectors and OpenAI for some gen tasks.
11:34 Jordan: that's common; Redwood integrates with Pinecone and other vector stores, you can also switch to our managed vector cache later. model-wise, where you use OpenAI for gen you can keep that and use Redwood for rerank if you like; some customers migrate to open models we host to reduce cost.
11:58 Liam: any rate limits we should be aware of on hosted?
12:03 Jordan: there are per-account rate limits but they are configurable with plan changes; we'll include recommended request batching to reduce egress.
12:15 Nina: okay let's talk PoC scope — what does a two-week PoC look like?
12:20 Priya: typical two-week scope: ingest 10k documents, run embeddings with 2 models, run retrieval + rerank on your 1k labeled queries, compute nDCG and click-sim metrics, provide a report and tuning recommendations. we can also demo Redwood Console dashboards.
12:40 Maria: sounds good; cost estimates?
12:43 Jordan: i'll model a small projection for that PoC and include it in the pricing doc.
12:50 Maria: any red flags on our side? we need SSO and at-rest encryption.
12:55 Jordan: covered — SSO via SAML for Hosted enterprise, encryption at rest, and we can discuss bringing your KMS for Private.
13:06 Maria: great.
13:08 Priya: quick note on rerank model updates — you can pin model versions and do canary rollouts with traffic splits in console.
13:20 Liam: operationally how do we troubleshoot misorders?
13:24 Priya: Console has per-query traces and token-level breakdowns; we can replay the query and inspect candidate features. we'll share an example trace.
13:40 Maria: ok last q — is there any sample data you need now?
13:45 Jordan: please send the labeled set and a small schema of your indexing pipeline; priya will take details on required formats.
13:55 Maria: we'll get that by Friday.
14:00 Jordan: perfect. recap and next steps: we'll send pricing + security pack + quickstart + sample code and propose a PoC scoping call. action items in the notes. thanks everyone.
14:12 Maria: thanks all.

END: 45-minute call (approx).
